findings.summary: Manifest, lockfile, and Next build/start scripts are present; no undeclared package imports were found in config files and the first 20 source files checked. Build was not executed.

Store, seller, admin, checkout, and payment flows exist, but local Razorpay mode variables are missing, several footer links target absent pages, and live inventory/order subscriptions and supplier automation were not found.
findings.fix: Complete payment configuration and the missing business workflows before production launch.

findings.summary: The app has a standard Next.js Node start path, but Firebase is a core cloud dependency and there is no Azure deployment scaffold or health endpoint.
findings.fix: Choose the hosting target; migrate Firebase services before continuing an Azure-only deployment workflow.

warnings.summary: Razorpay mode selectors are absent from the current .env.local configuration.
warnings.detail: RAZORPAY_MODE, RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET_MODE, and RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET_MODE are not set in .env.local or the current process environment. The application requires explicit compatible modes, so online payment setup/webhook requests will fail configuration validation until these are configured.
warnings.fix: Set the Razorpay mode variables to match the intended credentials in local/deployment secrets; do not commit secret values.

warnings.summary: Footer navigation links to pages that are not present in the app route tree.
warnings.detail: No route files were found for /shipping-policy, /returns-refunds, /faq, /contact, /seller/guidelines, or /seller/dropship-faq. These links will lead users to not-found pages, and the repository does not currently provide these customer/seller policy pages.
warnings.fix: Create the linked policy/support/seller-guidance pages or remove/replace the links before launch.

warnings.summary: Live inventory and order status updates are not implemented as realtime subscriptions.
warnings.detail: No Firestore onSnapshot listeners were found. The product pages use 60-second revalidation, account/order data is fetched through request-based APIs, and checkout polls payment status every 15 seconds; users should not expect immediate live catalog, stock, order, or shipment updates.
warnings.fix: If live updates are a product requirement, add Firestore subscriptions or an explicit server push/polling strategy for inventory and order milestones.

warnings.summary: Dropship fulfillment appears seller-managed rather than integrated with suppliers or carriers.
warnings.detail: Seller fulfillment endpoints accept manually entered carrier, tracking number/URL, and delivery milestones. No supplier feed/order-forwarding or carrier tracking API integration was found. The current implementation can support manual multi-seller fulfillment, but not automated end-to-end dropshipping.
warnings.fix: Confirm manual seller fulfillment is intended, or integrate the chosen supplier and carrier systems for catalog/stock sync, order forwarding, and tracking events.

warnings.summary: The sample Firebase project in .env.example differs from the Firebase CLI default.
warnings.detail: .env.example contains the sample project identifier casaio-app, while .firebaserc selects a different default project. The current .env.local identifiers were checked and match the CLI default, but a fresh setup copied from the example could point the app at a different Firebase project than the one receiving rule deployments.
warnings.fix: Replace sample project identifiers with explicit placeholders or align the example with the intended Firebase CLI project.

warnings.summary: The project does not declare its supported Node.js version.
warnings.detail: The local runtime is Node.js 22.16.0, but package.json has no engines field. A deployment host should be pinned to a Next-compatible Node.js runtime rather than relying on its default.
warnings.fix: Declare and configure the supported Node.js version in package.json and the selected hosting platform.

warnings.summary: No dedicated health endpoint was found.
warnings.detail: No /health or /healthz API route exists in the source tree. This does not prevent local startup, but a deployment health probe would need a suitable route or a configured storefront probe.
warnings.fix: Add a lightweight health endpoint or configure the hosting platform to probe a route that exists.
